question: Who is the presiding officer of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vice President**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The presiding officer of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) in India is the **Vice President**.
 
• The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• In the absence of the Vice President, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides over the sessions.
 
• The Vice President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament.
 
• The Vice President's role in the Rajya Sabha is crucial for maintaining order and decorum during debates and ensuring the smooth functioning of the house.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Rajya Sabha** is the upper house of India's bicameral Parliament, with representatives elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies and Electoral college for Union Territories.
 
• The Rajya Sabha represents the states and union territories of India and ensures federal equilibrium by protecting the interests of the states.
 
• The **Vice President** serves a term of five years but can be re-elected any number of times.
 
• The Vice President can also act as the President of India when there is a vacancy in the office of the President or when the President is unable to discharge his/her duties.
 
• The Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved, and it is a permanent body, with one-third of its members retiring every two years.
